$comment: Ratcheted ceilings on the surfaces this campaign exists to shrink.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The campaign produced 132 plan documents and one
mechanism that never failed: EXPECTED_HOST_IMPORT_COUNT, a number in the
repo asserted against a measurement of the built artifact. Every import
change hit it. Meanwhile fork TypeScript grew by 2,867 lines over the same
period with nothing to catch it, and nobody noticed for weeks. Documents
are advisory; a number a test asserts is not.
HOW THE RATCHET WORKS. Exceeding a ceiling fails: the surface grew.
Falling more than `slack` below it ALSO fails, asking you to lower the
ceiling in the same commit. That is what banks a reduction permanently --
without it, one lane's deletion silently funds the next lane's growth.
WHAT A CEILING IS NOT. It is not a goal. Every `target` below is far under
its ceiling, and the gap is the work. See docs/plans/2026-09-11-MASTER-PLAN.md.
LANE CLOSURE. `lanes` below binds each lane's status to measurements. A lane
marked `closed` whose conditions are unmet fails; a lane marked `open` whose
conditions are all met ALSO fails, saying to close it. Lane status therefore
cannot be asserted in prose -- which is what every previous attempt did, and
why drift was only ever caught when a human happened to ask.
A lane whose completion is not a number says so with `manual` and a reason.
That is honest; silence is not.
CHECKLIST CLOSURE is weaker than a measurement and is labelled as such. A
tick is self-reported. Its value is that the instances are enumerated, so a
lane cannot be closed by forgetting one.
CHARACTERIZATION is gated too. A lane must carry an End state, a floor, an
Increments list, Acceptance evidence and Known hazards before it is
dispatchable. A lane legitimately missing one declares `sectionsExempt` with
a reason -- because the failure this file exists to end is a status asserted
in prose that nothing checks, and that applies to its own sections first.
MEASURE CHANGE 2026-09-12 -- the seven TypeScript line surfaces count CODE
lines (neither blank nor purely a comment), not total lines. They exist to
stop TypeScript IMPLEMENTATION growing, because the goal is to move
implementation into Rust and the fork-module, and a total-line ceiling cannot
tell an added function from an added paragraph of explanation.
It failed a real commit that did the right thing: lane F's fm_capture_intern
collapse removed four per-type module exports and three host marshalling
wrappers -- fork TypeScript CODE fell 5 lines -- and the gate rejected it
because the commit also explained the collapse in 20 lines of comment. The
first response was to compress the explanation until the number went down.
That is the metric shaping the code instead of measuring it, so the metric
changed. A comment now costs nothing, which is the intended incentive: this
campaign's expensive defects are consistently the ones nobody wrote down.
Ceilings and targets were re-baselined in the same change. Targets were
scaled by each surface's own code/total ratio (~0.80), so a target keeps the
meaning it had: what fraction of this surface should survive. Targets of 0
stay 0.

forkTypeScript.why:
The MODULE-FACING half of stage 2: everything that places, instantiates and talks to the co-resident fork-module. BANKED at its measurement 2026-09-12 by maintainer decision, replacing the headroom ceiling of 250. That headroom was approved for exactly this half and the half is complete -- fork-module-host-capabilities.ts (65) plus fork-module-instance.ts (184) -- so leaving the ceiling above what exists would be the unbanked slack this file's preamble says funds the next lane's growth. SCOPE NARROWED at the same time: this used to measure every host/src/fork-*.ts and vfork-*.ts, which mixed a finished population with an unstarted one, and a ceiling over both cannot be read. The platform half now has its own surface, forkPlatformTypeScript, for the same reason forkModuleEntryPoints was split by purpose (see docs/plans/2026-09-12-lane-f-census.md section 10). TARGET EQUALS CEILING because this half is done: it is a floor to hold, not a gap to close. Every entry it contains is argued as a Wasm capability limit in the file itself -- placement cannot move into a side module, which does not choose where it is placed. Grounded against crates/host-native, which does the same work in 142 code lines (census sections 11, 15, 17 and 18).

RAISED 249 -> 419 on 2026-09-13 for `host/src/fork-module-backend.ts`, and the raise says something about the old number: this surface was declared DONE with target == ceiling while its LARGEST member sat in the attic. 249 measured an incomplete population, the same structural error `forkPlatformTypeScript`'s glob had. The backend is the module-facing half by definition -- it is the host's calls into the co-resident module. 

What it replaces is the argument for the number: 170 code lines against the 1239-line wrapper it supersedes, an 86% reduction. Two things shrank it -- the module folded eleven counter exports into one `fm_stats(field)` and the host wrapper never followed, so eight one-line accessors became one `stat()`; and half the old surface served the capture/replay orchestration the module took over. Methods come back when a caller needs one. 

Target equals ceiling again, deliberately: this is a floor to hold. If it rises without a caller appearing in `worker-main.ts`, that is the anticipation the 1239 lines were made of.

BANKED 419 -> 418 on 2026-09-13, the same day the maintainer set 419. The table-mutation commit needed a `channelBase` option (+2 lines, because a borrowed fork child cannot derive its channel from the archive control address). Rather than raise a just-decided ceiling by two, `stat()` lost its local 'is that a real field?' check: `fm_stats` answers -1 for a field it does not have, and the module is the authority on which fields exist. That check was a second opinion on the same question -- the duplication this lane removed from the GC codec and the exception codec -- so it should not have been there. Net -1.

RAISED 418 -> 433 on 2026-09-13, for two things the maintainer-approved `__wpk_fork_host_func_identity` made necessary. Three lines bind it in `instantiateForkModule`. The other twelve are a COMPLETENESS CHECK: before instantiating, every `env` function the artifact imports must be bound, or the host fails with the import's NAME. 

That check is here because its absence was a real defect, not a hypothetical. Adding the import broke this file's own tests, and the failure arrived as `LinkError: Import #10 ... requires a callable` -- an index, not a name. The guest side of the same contract has been complete by construction since `buildForkGuestImports`; the module's own host obligation had no equivalent, so the two directions were held to different standards. 

Placed BEFORE instantiation deliberately: the first version ran after, where the `LinkError` has already fired and the check can never speak. Perturbing it by removing the binding now fails with 'does not bind: __wpk_fork_host_func_identity'.

RAISED 433 -> 457 on 2026-09-13 for `sealCaptureAndSerialize` and a lazy `exports` getter, and the reason is a correction to how this file was rewritten. The rewrite's rule was 'methods come back when a caller needs one' -- and I checked only `worker-main.ts` for callers. 

A TEST is a caller. `fork-module-backend-coarse-failures` exercises the seal path specifically to prove a failed seal raises a TYPED `ContinuationAllocationError` rather than a generic throw that traps the worker. That test was failing and I had not noticed, because the gated runs used a hand-picked file list. Its absence from `worker-main` proves nothing: worker-main's caller for it is in the attic'd cluster, so 'no caller' was an artifact of the cluster being down. 

The lazy getter is the other half: `exports` is now read on demand so the resume-catalog cap check genuinely runs BEFORE any export is touched, which is what that same test asserts and what lets it prove the boundary with a stand-in instance.

RAISED 457 -> 484 on 2026-09-13 for `bindActivationDrive`, the second piece of the cluster port. It replaces `forkGcCodecProviderFromInstance` (about 90 attic lines) with 27: the old one bound five guest exports into a JavaScript object the HOST then called, and the module calls them now, so a host only has to put them where the module can reach -- a reference-typed `Table.set`, which is a genuine floor because Rust cannot hold a funcref. 

The five slot offsets are duplicated from `fork-codec`'s `drive_plan` and pinned against it, because binding the wrong slot makes the module call the wrong guest function with arguments that look right -- an allocate driven as a fill. Nothing traps; the child is simply rebuilt wrong. The stride is pinned for the same reason: a host growing by a smaller one leaves later activations overlapping earlier ones.

workerMainTypeScript.why:
Holds the fork drive loop. 6,083 -> 7,536 across the campaign; every fine-grained fm_* call leaves a host-side seeding and base-arithmetic loop behind by construction. Re-baselined 2026-09-12 from total lines to CODE lines: ceiling 7499 -> 5958, target 3000 -> 2400. Same code, a measure that counts implementation.

BANKED 5958 -> 5906 on 2026-09-13. The cluster port removed the host's two remaining decodes of module-owned formats from this file: the GC and exception codec DESCRIPTORS. Neither was needed -- the host already locates both sections and hands the module their raw bytes, and the host-exception owner (the smallest activation that DECLARED an exception codec) falls out of which activations have a section, not out of a decoded descriptor. 

This is the direction this file is supposed to move, so the reduction is banked rather than left as slack for the next addition to spend.

sffsTypeScript.why: The SFFS block filesystem is implemented twice: 3,752 lines here against 3,727 in sffs.rs + sffs_write.rs + sffs_deferred.rs, same superblock geometry, same allocators, same magic. Target is zero because one of the two must go and the kernel owns the format. Re-baselined 2026-09-12 from total lines to CODE lines: ceiling 3716 -> 3047, target 0 -> 0. Same code, a measure that counts implementation.

memoryFsTypeScript.why: The other half of the 12,198-line TypeScript filesystem the lane V text names and no register measured. MemoryFileSystem backs `/` on every machine and implements stat, statfs, pathconf, dirents, open flags and ST_NOSUID setuid handling in the host, against 1,724 lines of tmpfs.rs in the kernel. Target is 0 because lane V's end state says the host supplies nothing inside the image body; the V6 census is the deliverable that would prove any of it is floor, and until that census runs the 0 is an assertion of the plan's end state, not a measured floor. If the census finds real floor here, this target gets revised in the open with that evidence attached. Re-baselined 2026-09-12 from total lines to CODE lines: ceiling 8501 -> 7473, target 0 -> 0. Same code, a measure that counts implementation.

hostImportFunctions.measure: env.host_* function imports of the built kernel; see EXPECTED_HOST_IMPORT_COUNT
hostImportFunctions.why: V4, the primary goal: how many functions a new host must implement. Already asserted against the built artifact in crates/host-native; restated here so one file carries every surface. A raw import-ENTRY count reads 73 because env.memory is an entry -- say which you counted.

sffsModuleEntryPoints.measure: pub extern "C" fn sm_* declared in crates/sffs-module/src/lib.rs
sffsModuleEntryPoints.why: Banked at its measured value the moment it reached 19, not left to grow unwatched. This is the image builders' ABI, and every entry point is a call a builder makes and a shape the module must keep. The target is NOT 0: unlike forkModuleEntryPoints, these are not fine-grained steps of one operation that a coarse entry could replace -- they are distinct filesystem operations a builder genuinely performs, and the census measured 24 MemoryFileSystem methods that 19 already cover. The target is 'does not grow without an argument'. Two entries were deliberately NOT added while building this: the archive length rides in sm_register_lazy_file rather than an sm_declare_archive of its own, because a member is useless without it; and the container is emitted by sm_export_image_read rather than an sm_save_image, because a bare body is not an image.

forkModuleHostImports.measure: fork-module imports a host must satisfy (functions + reference-typed tables, excluding PIC linking); see EXPECTED_FORK_MODULE_HOST_IMPORT_COUNT
forkModuleHostImports.why:
V4, the primary goal, and the half of it that had NO gate. EXPECTED_HOST_IMPORT_COUNT pins the KERNEL's obligation and has never let an import through unnoticed; the fork-module is a separate artifact with its own imports that every host must also satisfy, and nothing asserted them. An import was added to it on 2026-09-12 (env.__wpk_fork_host_ref_identity, maintainer-approved) and no ceiling moved -- precisely the shape this file's preamble says the ratchet exists to prevent. THE GOAL IS NOT A SMALL NUMBER FOR ITS OWN SAKE: it is that host responsibilities stay few, CLEARLY DEFINED, and THIN to implement, with the shared Wasm module doing everything else. This surface measures the 'few and clearly defined' half; the 'thin' half is measured by the TypeScript line surfaces above. SCOPE: the built artifact declares 10 import entries. Five are position-independent-code linking boilerplate any --pie side module has (env.memory, __indirect_function_table, __stack_pointer, __memory_base, __table_base), supplied mechanically by a host that knows nothing about fork; counting them would overstate the obligation and make the number move for non-fork reasons. They are pinned separately by EXPECTED_FORK_MODULE_PIC_IMPORT_COUNT. The five counted here are each a Wasm CAPABILITY FLOOR, not a design choice: resolve_externref (Wasm cannot manufacture an externref), __wpk_fork_host_ref_identity (ref.eq validates only on eqref, there is no ref.hash, and no cast rescues a host reference into the eq hierarchy), and the three reference-typed catalog/drive tables (Rust cannot declare or hold one). TARGET EQUALS CEILING because no entry has been shown reducible; if one ever is, both fall. The host-native test also asserts the NAMES, since a swap that keeps the count equal still changes what every host implements, and it compares every fork-module artifact on disk -- build-wasm.sh stages into local-binaries/ and host/wasm/ but the resolver reads local-binaries/source-only-v1/ FIRST, so a disagreement means a host would load something other than what was just built (master-plan H-9). That disagreement was real on this gate's first run.

RAISED 5 -> 6 on 2026-09-13 for `env.__wpk_fork_host_func_identity`, MAINTAINER-APPROVED and conditional on the native host being able to supply it -- a condition answered with a test, not an argument (`a_native_host_can_identify_funcrefs`: `Func::to_raw` is stable per function, and a wasmtime import can take a `funcref`). 

What it buys: the module now serves `__wpk_fork_ref_encode_funcref` (unserved 6 -> 5) and it is the missing piece for `table_mutation_commit`. Wasm cannot do this for itself -- `ref.eq` validates only on `eqref` and the reference hierarchies are disjoint, measured in census section 58 -- so this is a genuine capability, not glue that could have stayed in the module. The HOST answers only 'are these the same function?'; the scan over the merged catalog, the slot-to-activation resolution, the ordinal, and the refusal of an uncatalogued function are all the module's. 

Target moves with the ceiling: 6 is the floor to hold, not a gap to close.

parseShebangReferences.why: Shebang is a kernel feature on every real Unix: execve(2) substitutes the interpreter. POSIX does not specify it at all and only requires libc's execvp family to fall back to sh on ENOEXEC, so a libc-only implementation is a divergence rather than a simplification. The lane is done when the host no longer parses it.

setuidLazyWithoutDigest.measure: packages with mode 4755 that ship lazy while the rootfs manifest emitter writes no digest for lazy outputs
setuidLazyWithoutDigest.why: sudo and sudo-lite ship setuid-root as lazy references fetched by URL with length as the only check. Bytes of the same length from a substituting host, a poisoned cache or a network position execute as root inside the guest.

kernelWorkerTypeScript.why: The single largest file in the host and the one every lane contends for. **Target validated by the K1 census, no longer provisional**: crates/host-native's guest.rs does the same job — fork, exec, clone, the blocking-retry pump — in 13,577 lines, against CentralizedKernelWorker's 29,975. The 12,000 target was guessed as 'roughly a third' and the native host independently lands near it. Note the measurement hazard: moving code inside this file shifts V8 parse and compile for unrelated functions, which was visible in the select A/B. Re-baselined 2026-09-12 from total lines to CODE lines: ceiling 32718 -> 26495, target 12000 -> 9700. Same code, a measure that counts implementation.

unguardedLayoutModules.measure: process_layout modules whose C-side _Static_asserts are not anchored to a generated KANDELO_ macro
unguardedLayoutModules.why: Lane G. **Measure corrected twice while implementing G1, and the second correction retracts a claim in the first.** (1) It originally counted modules the generated header DELIVERS as #defines, which extending the emitter would have driven to 0 while guarding nothing (H-2). (2) The replacement said 'no struct-layout assert exists anywhere in libc' — WRONG: libc/musl-overlay/arch/wasm32posix/bits/stat.h has 8, missed because they use __builtin_offsetof. The real defect is sharper: those 8 asserts compare C against **hand-written literals** (112, 32, 40...), not against the Rust authority, so 0 of 15 modules are anchored to the generated constants. The overlay header states in prose 'The complete layout MUST match crates/shared/src/process_layout.rs' and nothing enforces it — two sources agreeing by convention, the campaign's recurring shape. statx is the proven instance: stx_dev_minor was never written.

kernelHostImportTypeScript.why: The implementation behind lane I's 72 host imports; its host_* definitions span 3,771 of 4,775 lines. **Target re-derived by the I/X surface census (docs/plans/2026-09-11-lane-i-x-surface-census.md), which refuted the guessed 1,200**: host-native supplies the same surface through 71 linker.func_wrap calls spanning 7,646 lines of guest.rs, so there is no evidence the implementations shrink to 1,200. Lane I's real lever is the NUMBER of imports, gated separately by hostImportFunctions (72 -> 40). This target is arithmetic on that reduction — 4,774 x (40/72) — a consequence of the lane succeeding rather than an independent goal, and it is not a measurement. Re-baselined 2026-09-12 from total lines to CODE lines: ceiling 4774 -> 3822, target 2650 -> 2100. Same code, a measure that counts implementation.

hostKernelPlumbingTypeScript.measure: code lines (non-blank, non-comment) of host/src/kernel-scratch.ts, kernel-entry-gate.ts, process-memory.ts and worker-protocol.ts
hostKernelPlumbingTypeScript.why: Lane L. What a wasmtime host builds around the imports: entry serialization, capacity-carrying scratch views, process memory layout and the worker wire. **Target set by the L1 census (docs/plans/2026-09-11-lane-l1-census.md), not provisional.** The census raised it from a guessed 1,500 to a derived 3,600: ~428 lines are JavaScript self-defence a native host never writes, worker-protocol.ts (429) is JS-host structural because host-native uses native threads, and the re-entrancy gate stays because Rust gets it from the borrow checker and JavaScript cannot. What actually moves is duplicated knowledge — one process-memory layout, one bounds-check rule, and a generated scratch pointer table. Re-baselined 2026-09-12 from total lines to CODE lines: ceiling 5853 -> 4734, target 3600 -> 2900. Same code, a measure that counts implementation.

imageBuilderFilesystemImporters.measure: files under images/ importing host/src/vfs/memory-fs or sharedfs-vendor
imageBuilderFilesystemImporters.why: Lane Y, set by the Y1 census (docs/plans/2026-09-11-lane-y1-census.md). It replaces a line-count surface that measured the wrong thing: the builders' 13,502 lines are overwhelmingly recipes — which packages go in the LAMP image, how WordPress is preinstalled — and that product configuration stays. A line target invited deleting exactly the wrong lines. This counts the coupling instead, which is the fact lane V is blocked on: memory-fs.ts cannot be deleted while 36 builder files import it. Goes to 0 exactly when the lane is done.

hostPeerDuplicateDeclarations.measure: declaration names appearing in both halves of the three browser-/node- pairs
hostPeerDuplicateDeclarations.why: Lane E. Counts declaration names present in both halves of a browser-/node- pair, excluding members destructured from the shared createProcessLifecycle factory. **Target corrected from a guessed 12 to a derived 29 by the E3 audit (2026-09-12).** The 21 same-named worker-entry declarations were read one at a time: 4 are `let` MODULE STATE initialised from shared constants (maxPages, initReady, defaultThreadSlots, processMemoryAllocator) which cannot be shared because each host needs its own instance, and 17 differ for platform reasons — vforkMechanismTraceEnabled reads process.env in Node and a runtime message in the browser, which has no env vars. None is duplication to remove. The floor is 21 worker-entry + 6 genuinely-different protocol types + 2 message unions = 29.

artifactTierPathSpellings.measure: independent production spellings of the local-binaries/source-only-v1 tier path
artifactTierPathSpellings.why: Lane R, set by the R1 census. Replaces a line-count surface that would be satisfied by deleting policy that is not duplicated and untouched by fixing the duplication that is. host-native's equivalent of the 4,020-line TypeScript resolver is ten lines; what duplicates is the tier list and its order, spelled 8 times across the writer (xtask local-build, 7) and both readers. The drift already cost 39 of 53 host-native tests against a tree where the build had just succeeded.

sessionHandMaintainedSyscallNames.why: Lane W, set by the W1 census. A hand-maintained syscall-name table sitting beside a generated one: ABI_SYSCALL_NAMES has 233 entries, this copy has 137. 96 syscalls render in the UI as syscall_NNN, and 2 names actively disagree (129 statfs vs statfs64, 130 fstatfs vs fstatfs64). The comment justifying the copy cites avoiding a heavyweight kernel-worker import, but the generated table lives in host/src/generated/abi.ts, a leaf module with no Node-only imports.

sessionKernelFormatParsers.measure: hand-written parsers of kernel-emitted text formats in web-libs/kandelo-session
sessionKernelFormatParsers.why: Lane W. parseMaps, parseMounts, parseProcEntry, parseStatusBytes and parseRangeSize parse /proc/<pid>/maps, /proc/mounts and /proc/<pid>/status with hand-written regexes. The kernel holds this data structured, serialises it to text, and the UI re-derives it with nothing binding the two. Lane G's failure mode in the UI layer.

buildFreshnessDigestsOutsideRust.measure: non-test scripts under scripts/ computing a build-freshness digest
buildFreshnessDigestsOutsideRust.why: Lane U, set by the U1 census. Replaces two line-count surfaces that measured size — the axis the lane's own text says is wrong — and would have been satisfied by rewriting loud, harmless test runners. This counts the tier that can silently produce a wrong artifact. The archetype is build-step-input-hash.sh: a content-identity cache-key primitive written in shell, consumed by build-host.sh, build-rootfs.sh AND tools/xtask/src/local_build.rs, and mirroring a second shell script that folds the same logic. The repo has already served a stale kernel from a cache key that omitted an input. Target is 6, not 0: release verification and CI deployment checks legitimately compute digests in shell and fail loudly.

kernelWorkerClassMethods.why: Lane K, added by the K1 census. 91.6% of kernel-worker.ts is one class: 522 methods over 29,780 lines. A line-count gate alone permits shuffling code between methods of the same god class while nothing improves; method count in the largest class does not. The lane is decomposition, not migration — the 85 syscalls the host dispatches genuinely need host services, and host-native dispatches them too.

forkGuestImportsUnserved.measure: canonical fork imports in the crates/shared ProgramArtifactImport table that crates/fork-module does not export under the same name
forkGuestImportsUnserved.why: The guest declares 46 fork imports. Each one the fork-module exports VERBATIM can be wired with a nameless loop -- host-native already does this for the five frame imports. Each one exported under a different spelling (fm_ref_gc_route for __wpk_fork_ref_gc_route) forces a mapping table back into the host, which is the hand-maintained-knowledge-beside-a-generator defect three censuses in this campaign have found. Target 0 is the point at which the JS host layer is pure wiring. The 19 -> 18 step, banked 2026-09-12, is __wpk_fork_ref_exn_define: the one define in the family that needs nothing but guest linear memory, because fork-instrument's exception codec stages scalars AND the payload recipe ids into a single scratch span before the call. GROUNDED BREAKDOWN of the remaining 18, read at each emission site in crates/fork-instrument rather than inferred from signatures: 5 are the module_state_table_* mutation group, blocked on an undefined journal format (maintainer decision). Of the other 13: TWO need no new fm_* entry at all (gc_define and gc_provenance_end are pure scalars over guest memory) but both are coupled to the provenance registry and must land with it -- serving gc_define alone would bake in 'provenance is always absent', which is only true because nothing serves provenance_begin yet. TEN each need an injected wasm shim backed by a new fm_* helper: seven because the value arrives in a reference-typed TABLE slot (gc_capture_layout, gc_broker_encode, gc_provenance_begin, gc_provenance_ref, exn_lookup, exn_claim, exn_broker_encode), two because they must THROW so the guest's try_table catches the exnref -- the emitter puts `unreachable` after the call, so returning normally is a bug (exn_ingress_throw, exn_broker_throw_recipe) -- and one because it is externref in and externref out (provenance_externref). The LAST one, encode_funcref, is the only remaining import that grows the HOST contract: it takes the funcref as a parameter and must return its recipe id, wasm cannot compare funcrefs, and funcref is not a subtype of anyref, so the approved __wpk_fork_host_ref_identity cannot serve it -- it needs a funcref-identity host import of its own. So the tranche is about +11 fm_ entries against a ceiling of 54, plus one new host import. That collision is what has to be resolved before it can land. The 18 -> 15 step, banked 2026-09-12, is the constructor-provenance trio (__wpk_fork_ref_gc_provenance_begin/_ref/_end). begin and end are pure scalars and needed no shim at all; only _ref does, because it moves the guest's staged seed from the transit table into a module-owned WITNESS table. Crucially it needs no host import and no reference identity: the witness is keyed by (layout, ordinal), both plain integers the guest already passes, which is what keeps it off the allocation hot path. See docs/plans/2026-09-12-lane-f-census.md sections 21 and 22. The 15 -> 13 step, banked 2026-09-12, is __wpk_fork_ref_exn_lookup and __wpk_fork_ref_exn_claim, both pure Rust with no shim and no host surface. Lookup always reports NOT FOUND, so every catch takes a fresh recipe. That is a measured decision, not a shortcut: NOTHING can dedup an exception. Wasm cannot -- `exn` is a disjoint hierarchy, so ref.eq on two exnrefs does not validate, an exnref cannot enter an anyref table, and no cast rescues one into the eq hierarchy; only ref.is_null accepts an exnref at all. And a JS host cannot -- an exnref VALUE cannot cross into a JS import, which compiles and instantiates then throws TypeError at the first call. The same limitation is why it costs nothing: a guest cannot observe that two exnrefs are distinct either, and payloads still dedup through the normal identity path, so two exception recipes share their payload objects. Measured with wasm-tools validate against a positive AND a negative control; see census sections 28a, 28b and 29. The 13 -> 12 step is __wpk_fork_ref_exn_broker_encode, the unknown-tag path, served as a LOUD REFUSAL: EOPNOTSUPP and a poisoned recipe. A foreign exception is opaque on every axis -- its payload needs catch_ref against a tag this module does not have, it cannot be identified, and it cannot be handed to a host to inspect. Real handling means routing to the activation whose codec owns the tag, which needs a capture-side drive that does not exist (F3). The refusal is structural rather than a gated placeholder BECAUSE no gate signal is exported -- fm_stats has no gated counter -- so a placeholder would let the child rebuild the i31(0) sentinel where an exception had been and say nothing. The poisoned value is not a valid recipe id, so any edge naming it is rejected at define and the capture cannot seal. That restriction (no fork while a foreign exception is live) is stated, not hidden, and is not a regression: an unserved import leaves the same case to a host that cannot inspect the exception either. Census section 30. The 12 -> 11 step is __wpk_fork_ref_gc_define, and it is the first time the module DRIVES THE GUEST to capture rather than to replay. Constructor-provenance witnesses are interned lazily inside it, through an injected shim that stages the witness in the anyref transit slot and call_indirects the guest's own __wpk_fork_ref_gc_encode_slot at drive slot 11 -- so the module gets a recipe for a reference Rust can neither hold nor describe. The recipe is CACHED per witness, since a witness is shared by every object of its layout. §21 established gc_define must not be served without this: alone it would pass no provenance for every object and bake in 'provenance is always absent'. No host import was added and no target-0 ceiling moved -- the shim is reached through the placeholder-import pattern, so the emitted module carries no unresolved import. Census sections 38, 39, 40 and 41. The 11 -> 10 step is __wpk_fork_ref_gc_capture_layout, answered by driving the guest's own TYPE-TEST probe at drive slot 12 rather than by keeping a map. A layout is a per-OBJECT fact -- two objects of one base type can be made by different constructors -- so the witness trick that made provenance bounded does not apply, and recording it per object is the unbounded storage problem of census §20. Asking the guest costs nothing and stores nothing: the value is already in the transit slot and the guest's generated codec ref.tests it, returning (type_ordinal << 32) | layout_id. The caller's static layout argument is deliberately NOT trusted over the type test. Census §42. The 10 -> 9 step is __wpk_fork_ref_gc_broker_encode, the cross-activation path: a structurally canonical GC value can enter through another dynamically loaded module, whose codec is the one that can encode it. The module cannot inspect a reference, so it ASKS each registered activation's codec through the drive table and routes to the first CLAIMANT -- probe then encode, both the guest's own generated functions. Bounded by the number of registered activations, not by objects. An unclaimed value is EOPNOTSUPP and a poisoned recipe rather than an invented one, the same structural refusal the exception broker uses. Census §43.

forkGuestObjectImportsUnserved.measure: non-function guest fork imports (tables, globals, the unwind tag) the fork-module does not define and export
forkGuestObjectImportsUnserved.why: A real fork-instrumented guest imports 51 env.__wpk_fork_* entries; the canonical ProgramArtifactImport table declares the 46 that are FUNCTIONS, because that struct carries params/results and cannot describe a table, global or tag. The other five were therefore invisible to forkGuestImportsUnserved. Counted separately because serving one is different work: a table or tag is DEFINED and exported by the module rather than implemented. __wpk_fork_ref_gc_transit and __wpk_fork_unwind are already served this way.

forkModuleInjectorHelpers.measure: fm_* entries called ONLY by crates/fork-module-inject (an injected wasm shim), never by a host
forkModuleInjectorHelpers.why: Internal implementation, NOT host surface. Each exists because the work is split across a boundary neither side can cross alone: the injected wasm shim is the only thing that can HOLD a reference, and Rust is the only thing that can hold a MAP or a counter. The shim calls the host import to turn its reference into an integer, then calls into Rust with that integer. A host never sees these, so they add nothing a host must implement. Currently 3: fm_drive_bump, fm_gc_identity_find, fm_gc_identity_claim. CEILING 15 IS A PRE-AUTHORIZED ENVELOPE, not a measurement: ten of the eighteen remaining guest imports each need one of these (seven read a reference-typed table slot, two must THROW so the guest's try_table catches the exnref, one is externref in and out), so this surface is EXPECTED to rise to about 15 as they land. Slack 12 is what lets 3 pass today without the ceiling being wrong. Exceeding 15 is a decision, not a rounding. Unlike every other entry here this one is not trying to reach zero -- the floor is however many such boundaries exist.

forkModuleEntriesWithoutProductionCaller.measure: fm_* entries no production host and no injector shim calls -- reached only by tests, or by nothing
forkModuleEntriesWithoutProductionCaller.why:
H-1 at scale: dead floor reads as complete. 27 of 54 entries are reached only by host/test, crates/fork-module/tests/*.mjs, or nothing at all. WHY THE TEST-ONLY AND NEVER-CALLED GROUPS ARE ONE NUMBER: ratcheting test-only entries separately would reward DELETING TESTS to make a ceiling pass, which is a perverse incentive a ratchet must not create. Merged, the only ways down are the two that are actually wanted -- wire an entry to a production caller, or delete the entry. Deleting its test moves it from test-only to never-called and changes nothing. NOT ALL OF THIS IS DEAD, and it must not be deleted to bank a reduction: fm_frame_{reserve,commit,peek,next}, fm_resume_peek, fm_set_activation_resume_catalog and fm_activation_module_buffer all take an explicit activation_id, where the guest-facing __wpk_fork_frame_* counterparts call the IDENTICAL *_impl with primary_activation(). They are the multi-activation (dlopen fork) variants -- a fork across N dynamically loaded libraries needs each activation's own resume catalog and frame cursor, because resume-slot numbering must match that activation's table by construction. Pending capability, not dead code. fm_abort is the one that is neither, and may be a live gap: it releases fork chunks without requiring the replay to have finished, its abort_impl is reachable from nowhere else, and its doc says it mirrors the JS backend's abort() -- which Phase 4 deleted. Whether host-native has an error route that leaks chunks is NOT established. COUNTED BY CALLER, NOT BY MENTION: the measure strips comments first. Without that, a doc comment naming an entry read as a caller -- one sentence of prose in host/src moved fm_gc_identity_find out of the injector-only bucket -- while string literals are deliberately KEPT, because host-native binds its drive surface by name inside one. Census: section 10.

NO LONGER RATCHETED ALONE from 2026-09-13: `forkModuleHostEntries` ratchets this bucket together with the host-called one, because a reconnection moves entries between them without adding anything. Slack is set to the ceiling so this stays MEASURED and visible -- its target of 0 is still the truth that an entry nothing calls is a defect -- without failing the build for a movement the paired ratchet already accounts for.

forkPlatformTypeScript.measure: code lines (non-blank, non-comment) of the thin layer this lane authors, named file by file
forkPlatformTypeScript.why: The PLATFORM half of stage 2: worker spawn, vfork address-space lifetime, cross-worker replay commit ordering, the host import runtime. Currently 0 -- this lane set all of it aside in attic/fork-typescript-do-not-use/ and none has been rewritten yet. CEILING 450 IS A PRE-AUTHORIZED ENVELOPE, not a measurement, granted 2026-09-12 on the same terms as the module half's 250 was: it must be BANKED to the real figure once the half stops moving, and a ceiling left above what exists is exactly the unbanked slack this file exists to prevent. Slack 450 is what lets 0 pass today. THE ESTIMATE IS SOFT AND LIKELY HIGH: census section 23 measured what each set-aside module actually depends on and found three of five are neither coordination nor floor -- fork-process-continuation alone is 1,471 lines of DRIVER LOOP that should collapse under the F3 coarsening rather than be rewritten, and fork-replay-gate's shared-i32 gate is expressible in wasm once it moves out of its own SharedArrayBuffer. Target 300 reflects that. The genuine floor here is narrow: worker creation, message transfer, and the async lifecycle the module cannot observe.

Target 300 reflects that. The genuine floor here is narrow: worker creation, message transfer, and the async lifecycle the module cannot observe.

TARGET SET TO 500 by the maintainer on 2026-09-13, replacing the 300 this file previously carried. That 300 was invented, not measured -- section 13 guessed ~450 and section 23 then showed most of the set-aside modules are not floor at all, so it was halved by judgment. The maintainer's instruction with the number: minimize use of the capacity, and if the floor genuinely needs more, do the work provisionally and RAISE IT WITH THEM rather than stopping. Read 500 as a stop-and-talk line, not an allowance to spend: the risk this target carries is that an invented budget becomes a budget that gets spent.

SCOPE NARROWED on 2026-09-13 from a glob over host/src/fork-*.ts to the three files this lane actually authors. The glob was correct while every other fork file was in the attic and wrong the moment any came back: it then counted newly written code and restored host floor as ONE number, which is the population mixing the maintainer had forkModuleEntryPoints split for. Restored floor now has its own surface, forkRestoredHostFloor.

forkRestoredHostFloor.measure: code lines (non-blank, non-comment) of host/src/fork-*.ts and vfork-*.ts, EXCLUDING fork-module-*.ts and the authored thin layer
forkRestoredHostFloor.rationale:
Host floor restored from the attic, BANKED at its measurement so it can only shrink. The 2026-09-12 sweep moved every host/src/fork-*.ts and vfork-*.ts aside by FILENAME. Nine of those files are not fork capture/replay logic at all -- they are process lifecycle (fork-replay-gate, vfork-lifetime), cross-worker host-import transport (fork-externref-import-mailbox, fork-host-import-runtime, fork-worker-import-exceptions, fork-worker-exception-capability), the externref broker the Rust-first contract names as floor (fork-reference-broker), and memory placement (vfork-workspace, fork-continuation). Keeping them in the attic broke 38 test files and 843 passing assertions for no gain. 

THE TARGET IS NOT MINE TO SET and is deliberately parked equal to the ceiling. Some of this should still shrink -- 1165 lines of externref mailbox and 796 of worker import exceptions are large for 'floor' -- but inventing a number here is precisely what the maintainer warned about: a target I invent becomes a budget I then spend. The ratchet already works with ceiling == target: this can only go down. 

Every file here is argued in docs/plans/2026-09-12-lane-f-census.md section 64, with its live consumers and why it is not capture logic. fork-module-state (3825 lines) was NOT restored for the opposite reason: it is a second implementation of the KFMS wire format the module owns, which is the decoder-drift hazard the campaign exists to remove.

RE-BANKED 3777 -> 3894 on 2026-09-13 for `fork-resume-catalog` (the tenth file, a 134-line reader of the host-known resume-catalog custom section that `fm_set_resume_catalog` requires the host to locate). This number moves ONLY while the attic audit is still running, and only ever by a file being RECLASSIFIED from the attic to floor -- never by a line being written. Once the audit is done it can only fall. A rise here from authored code would be the abuse this surface exists to prevent, and is distinguishable in the diff: a reclassification is a `git mv` with no content change, which is what both of these were.

forkModuleHostEntries.measure: fm_* entries in crates/fork-module/src/lib.rs that a production host calls, PLUS those nothing calls (the two buckets a reconnection moves entries between)
forkModuleHostEntries.rationale:
ONE ratchet over two buckets, by maintainer decision 2026-09-13, replacing the separately-ratcheted `forkModuleHostDriveEntries` (25) and this surface's own ceiling.

Splitting them was right while they moved independently. They stopped: reconnecting the thin layer gives an EXISTING entry a production caller, so it changes bucket and the two move equal and opposite. That happened three times in one day -- 25+21, 30+16, and once more -- total 46 every time, and each looked like a raise in isolation. Two of the day's ceiling moves would not have happened under this measure.

The sum falls only when the module ABSORBS work or an entry is deleted, which is what this surface was always about. Target 5 carries over from the old drive-entries surface: the inversion target is 3-5 coarse entries a host must call. Both halves are still measured and reported separately for visibility -- see `forkModuleEntriesWithoutProductionCaller`, whose own target of 0 still says a dead entry is a defect -- but neither is ratcheted alone.

The import obligation is a DIFFERENT and more expensive surface: see `forkModuleHostImports`.

F.title: fork control flow — invert, do not port

closure.note: Was `forkModuleHostDriveEntries`. That surface merged into `forkModuleHostEntries` on 2026-09-13 by maintainer decision: the host-called and no-production-caller buckets move equal and opposite when a reconnection gives an existing entry a caller, so the pair's total is the number that only falls when the module absorbs work. The closure condition is unchanged in substance -- at most 5 fm_* entries a host must call, with none left dead.

F.why: Inversion is done when the host calls a handful of coarse entries and no longer drives the sequence. Each fine-grained fm_* entry leaves a host-side seeding loop behind, so the entry count and the TypeScript line count fall together or neither has moved.

V.title: VFS image — one implementation of SFFS
V.why: The block filesystem is implemented twice at near-identical size. The lane closes when the TypeScript copy is gone, not when the Rust one works.

I.title: host import surface — V4
I.why: 28 of 72 imports are POSIX filesystem operations the kernel already implements for its own mounts. A host-backed mount needs roughly six calls. 40 is the ceiling to beat, not the goal.

P.title: platform honesty
P.why: Not reducible to one count: the defect is capability and state presented that do not exist. The checklist is SELF-REPORTED and says so -- it enumerates the instances so none can be waved through in prose, but a tick is a claim, and each must be backed by a test demonstrated failing against the old behaviour first.
P.whyExempt: A class of defect rather than a subsystem: there is no capability boundary to describe, so 'floor' has no meaning here.

X.title: process and exec
X.why: Closure is the kernel deciding what a spawn runs. parseShebang reaching zero is the measurable form; the probe traps today, so the panic is the blocker rather than the design. The processExecTypeScript surface added on 2026-09-11 was WITHDRAWN by the I/X surface census: it counted process-lifecycle.ts, which is the shared createProcessLifecycle implementation both worker entries call and which the E1 census credits as the consolidation that already happened. Shrinking it is not a goal. The exec-target authority has also already largely moved to the kernel (8 exports).

C.title: conformance
C.why: Closure is a failing-file-set comparison with no campaign-caused regression, not a total. Totals hide compensating changes, and the merge-base cannot produce a comparable set because its runner times out every guest-executing test.

S.title: setuid lazy references are fetched without integrity
S.why: Closure is that no setuid binary is fetched without its bytes being verified. Either the emitter records a digest for lazy outputs, or those packages stop shipping lazy.

M.title: shared-mapping cutover
M.why: Deferred by the maintainer out of #1350; resumes as a separate PR targeting its branch. Handoff at docs/plans/2026-09-11-lane-a-state-of-the-lane.md.
M.whyExempt: Deferred out of #1350. Its characterization lives whole in docs/plans/2026-09-11-lane-a-state-of-the-lane.md, written by the agent that did the diagnosis; duplicating it here would create the second authority this file exists to remove.

B.title: build and provisioning truthfulness
B.why: Closure is that a build which cannot produce a usable artifact says so, and that the documented provisioning path and the documented freshness gate agree. Neither is a count.

T.title: test hygiene
T.why: Closure is every host-suite failure attributed to a named cause. Blocked on a clean suite read rather than on work.

H.title: browser
H.why: Deprioritized by the maintainer. Closure is a browser pass plus curation, both of which are judgement rather than measurement.
H.whyExempt: Deprioritized by the maintainer, who asked to push implementation further before paying the cost of browser verification. Characterizing it now would plan work nobody intends to start.

K.title: kernel-worker.ts — one god class every lane contends for
K.why: The K1 census corrected the lane's framing: this is NOT the host's second syscall table. The 85 syscalls it dispatches are the ones needing a host service — worker creation, Atomics.wait blocking, shared memory — and host-native dispatches the same set. The defect is shape: 522 methods in one class, 29,975 lines, against guest.rs's 13,577 for the same responsibility.

G.title: ABI binding drift — all 15 layout modules anchored to generated constants
G.why: A layout constant with no static assert on the C side can drift from what musl expects and nothing notices. statx is the proven instance; 9 of 15 modules are equally exposed.

D.title: dead Rust floors
D.why: Five dead Rust modules beyond shared_mapping_policy were found and never characterized. A count is the wrong measure because the answer per module is either 'give it a caller' or 'delete it', and both reduce the same number. SELF-REPORTED checklist; a tick is a claim.
D.whyExempt: Dead code has no capability boundary to describe; the floor question belongs to whichever lane owns the subsystem each module was written for.

L.title: Host-kernel plumbing — what a wasmtime host writes beyond the imports
L.why: Goal V1 more than V4, which the L1 census established: a new host's burden here is already near zero — host-native proves it — but the same knowledge exists twice and the second copy was made by transcription (47 comments in host-native cite host/src/*.ts). Two transcribed copies drift and host #3 transcribes a third.

E.title: Node/browser peer divergence — shared types unified to the audited floor
E.why: Goal V1. CLOSED 2026-09-12 at the floor the E3 audit derived. The consolidation was already largely done before the lane started — the worker-entry pair shares 72 lifecycle members through a createProcessLifecycle factory — and what remained was 36 duplicated protocol declarations, now unified. The floor of 29 is 21 worker-entry declarations that are legitimately per-host (4 module-state lets, 17 platform differences), 6 genuinely-different protocol types, and 2 message unions. No category-three divergence was ever found: no bug one host fixed and the other did not.

R.title: Binary and artifact resolution — one declaration of the tier order
R.why: Goal V1. Not a resolver migration: host-native reimplemented ten lines, not 4,020. The tier list and its order are spelled 8 times across the writer and both readers, and that drift has already produced a measured failure. The right fix was already applied once inside TypeScript (binary-tiers.ts) and stopped at the language boundary.

Y.title: VFS image builders write the image format in TypeScript
Y.why: Goal V3, and a hard prerequisite for lane V. The Y1 census found the Rust side already covers nearly the whole builder contract across sffs_write.rs, sffs.rs and sffs_deferred.rs; the gaps are six image-level operations and three policy assertions, not a filesystem. Not a line-reduction lane — a decoupling lane.

W.title: web-libs session contracts a new host consumes
W.why: Goals V1 and V2. The W1 census found three populations, not two: the host contract, the browser product surface that stays, and a third the lane missed — hand-written parsers of kernel-emitted /proc formats plus a hand-maintained syscall table that is 96 entries short of the generated one and disagrees with it on two names.

U.title: Build automation in shell and MJS
U.why: Goal V2 and the repo's Rust-tools preference. Still does NOT serve V4 and stays ranked last. But the U1 census separates a cheap tier-1 subset (one Rust digest primitive replacing two shell copies, plus the manifest emitter lane S already needs) with already-realised failure modes, from the tier-2 bulk the census recommends not migrating.
